topics.description: A region is a geographic location; availability zones are isolated datacentres within it. Spreading across zones is the basic availability technique.

topics.description: Provider-operated components — databases, queues, caches — trading control for reduced operational burden.

topics.description: Web console, CLI, API and infrastructure-as-code are four ways to drive the same platform. All of them are audit-logged by the provider; what differs is reproducibility — console work leaves no artifact you can review, re-run or diff, while infrastructure-as-code adds declarative desired state and drift detection.

topics.description: The provider’s contractual commitment, typically an availability percentage with remedies if missed.
